name: The Beatles
hook: The band that turned the recording studio into an instrument, handed the Rolling Stones a hit, and then was sampled by the Beastie Boys without asking.
blurb: John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr came from Liverpool and became the most famous band in the world in the 1960s. They started as a beat group playing American rock and roll. In 1963 Lennon and McCartney finished a song in front of the Rolling Stones and gave it to them, and it became the Stones' first top-20 hit. On this map they matter less for their fame than as the band that made the studio a tool for writing music. By the mid-1960s, with their producer George Martin, they were making sounds nobody had heard: tape played backwards, loops, orchestras, and new machines like the Mellotron, which McCartney played on 'Strawberry Fields Forever'. Their tape loops and machine sounds are an ancestor of sampling, so it fits that the Beastie Boys sampled Abbey Road for Paul's Boutique; the Beatles' side is reported to have taken legal action over it. Their records have been among the hardest in popular music to clear for samples, which is why so few hip-hop records use them. The Beatles split in 1970.
